title: Countability of sphere homotopy classes for a countable simplicial set
statement: Use simplicial sets [def-weil-pbc-simplicial-set] and their geometric realization [def-cbc-enhanced-diagrams-cones]. For $n\geq0$ put $S^n=\{x\in\mathbb R^{n+1}:\sum_i x_i^2=1\}$ with its usual topology. Two continuous maps $S^n\to|A|$ are homotopic if they are the two endpoint maps of a continuous map $S^n\times[0,1]\to|A|$, with no fixed-basepoint condition. If a simplicial set $A$ has at most countably many simplices in total, then for every integer $n\geq0$ there are at most countably many such homotopy classes of continuous maps $S^n\to|A|$.

proof.text: Put $B=\operatorname{Ex}^{\infty}A$, with the explicit sequential-colimit construction of [lem-coef-ex-infinity-finite-products]. Here is the countability check for that construction. For each fixed $m$, the poset $\mathcal P_+([m])$ is finite. Every weakly increasing chain in it is a degeneracy of the strict chain obtained by deleting repetitions. A simplicial map $N(\mathcal P_+([m]))\to X$ is therefore determined by its values on the finitely many strict chains. If the total simplex set of $X$ is countable, these values belong to a finite product of countable sets, which is countable by coding finite tuples of natural numbers. Thus $(\operatorname{Ex}X)_m$ is countable; taking the countable union over $m$ proves that $\operatorname{Ex}X$ has countably many simplices in total. Induction gives the same assertion for $\operatorname{Ex}^rA$ for every $r$. The total simplex set of the degreewise sequential colimit $B$ is an image of the countable union of these total simplex sets, so it too is countable. The cited theorem also supplies that $B$ is Kan and that the canonical map $j:A\to B$ is a weak homotopy equivalence, meaning that $|j|$ is bijective on path components and isomorphic on every positive based homotopy group.

source.place: Construction 3.3.6.1 and Propositions 3.3.6.7 and 3.3.6.9; agent countability argument for the explicit construction.

proof.text: Fix $n\geq0$ and put $K=\partial\Delta^{n+1}$, whose simplices are the monotone maps to $[n+1]$ omitting a vertex, as in [lem-coef-realization-finite-limits]. Every such map factors as a surjection onto its ordered image followed by the injection of that image. Thus every simplex of $K$ is a degeneracy of one of the finitely many strictly increasing proper faces. A simplicial map $K\to B$ is determined by its values on those proper faces, so its set of choices injects into a finite product of the countable sets $B_r$ from step 1. Consequently $\operatorname{Hom}_{\mathrm{sSet}}(K,B)$ is countable. This includes $n=0$, when $K$ consists of two vertices and their degeneracies.

source.place: The boundary-simplex convention in §3.1 and the realized boundary-pair paragraph after Proposition 3.2.2; agent finite-tuple counting argument.

proof.text: Apply [lem-cbc-kan-realization-mapping-classes] with the arbitrary simplicial source $K$ and the Kan target $B$ obtained in step 1. It gives a bijection from the vertices of $\operatorname{Fun}(K,B)$ modulo the equivalence relation generated by edges to the free continuous homotopy classes $[|K|,|B|]$. These vertices are precisely the simplicial maps $K\to B$, so step 2 makes that quotient countable. By the boundary-pair clause of [lem-coef-realization-finite-limits], applied in dimension $n+1$, $|K|$ is homeomorphic to the usual $S^n$. Precomposing with that homeomorphism and its inverse identifies the free homotopy-class sets. Hence $[S^n,|B|]$ is countable.

source.place: Proposition 3.6.5.2 and Construction 3.6.5.1, on components; sphere identification from the cited boundary-pair theorem.

proof.text: The weak homotopy equivalence $|j|:|A|\to|B|$ of step 1 satisfies exactly the hypotheses of [lem-coef-sphere-mapping-weak-equivalence]. Therefore postcomposition induces a bijection on path components of $k\operatorname{Cont}(S^n,|A|)\to k\operatorname{Cont}(S^n,|B|)$. To identify these components with the homotopy relation in the statement, note that the Euclidean sphere is compact Hausdorff and locally compact. Apply [lem-coef-compact-open-currying] with parameter $[0,1]$ and compact domain $S^n$: paths in the compact-open mapping space correspond exactly to continuous maps $[0,1]\times S^n\to|A|$ with the specified endpoint maps, and likewise for $|B|$. Switching the two product factors gives the required $S^n\times[0,1]$ convention. Kification does not change these paths: by the definition of the k-space topology in [lem-coef-realization-finite-limits], any continuous map from the compact Hausdorff interval into a space remains continuous into its kification, since the inverse image of every k-open set is open; the converse follows since every original open set is k-open. Thus the component bijection is exactly $[S^n,|A|]\xrightarrow{\sim}[S^n,|B|]$, induced by postcomposition. Its right side is countable by step 3, proving the assertion. No basepoint or connectedness restriction has been imposed.
